name: The Consent of the Wired
creator: Dr. Amara Sundqvist-Obi, hosted under Axiom University Open Lecture Series
description: A long-form philosophy discussion podcast produced under the academic umbrella of Axiom University but distributed freely on both corporate and independent neural feed channels, making it unusually accessible for an academic production. Dr. Sundqvist-Obi and rotating guests — philosophers, neuroscientists, augmented-rights advocates, and occasionally the Gray Zone community organizers — engage with questions of personhood, memory continuity, and whether consent to BCI implantation can be meaningfully given in a society where BCI refusal constitutes economic exclusion. Episodes run between ninety minutes and three hours with no advertisement interruptions.
medium: neural feed audio / text-transcript physical zine edition
cultural_impact: The episode 'Can a Rented Mind Refuse?' became required reading in several underground synthetic-rights organizing spaces and is frequently cited in Seam Rights literature despite the show's academic origins.
controversy: Axiom University's corporate board attempted to pull funding after a 2209 episode in which a guest argued that mandatory BCI registration constituted a form of cognitive property seizure; Dr. Sundqvist-Obi published the board's internal memo in the following episode.
story_hooks: Dr. Sundqvist-Obi invites a guest who claims to have achieved genuine memory continuity across three consecutive BCI model replacements and wants to discuss what that means for identity — but the guest's story doesn't fully add up.

A Tier 1 community organizer appears on the show and delivers testimony that accidentally reveals information that could expose an illegal chrome operation; powerful people begin pressuring Dr. Sundqvist-Obi to scrub the episode.
The show receives an anonymous submission: a philosophical argument so rigorous and strange that Sundqvist-Obi suspects it was written by an augmented mind operating beyond standard parameters.
